comparator.name: Biology (Biologie)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted Biology OER 2026–27, articles 11–12 and current 2026–27 study guide; checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER specifies ten 6-EC compulsory first-year units, five 6-EC compulsory second-year units, two separate 6-EC obligatory restricted choices in periods one and two, and three 6-EC suggested choices in periods three, five and six instantiated with the first-listed eligible units. Year three has 30 EC genuinely open academic minor space, 6 EC Science Skills and a 24-EC Biology bachelor thesis. Zero-credit study/career orientation, lab safety and language assessment do not enter the 180 EC. The general prospective page still lists older first-year titles such as Bouwstenen van het leven and Systeembiologie and omits current credited modules; the adopted 2026–27 OER and study guide determine this pathway. Optional minors are not formal bachelor routes.

alternatives.label: Living systems from cells to ecosystems
alternatives.concept: Connects molecular and cellular biology, physiology, evolution, biodiversity and ecosystems with quantitative methods and both laboratory and environmental research. It follows the VU systems view across levels while UCR offers less specialised microbiology and fieldwork.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed course set gives substantial space to life and health sciences, ecology, evolution and biological data methods rather than claiming a single subfield.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offerings pass the enriched workbook. Introductory life, ecology, mathematics or sustainability courses precede relevant advanced work where scheduling permits; advisory progression has been reviewed.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution and environmental health
alternatives.concept: Studies biodiversity, evolutionary adaptation and ecosystem change through conservation, marine biology, climate science, delta environments and field-linked research. Human and public health provide a limited organism-level connection rather than the organising centre.
alternatives.labelReason: Ecology and environmental courses dominate the curriculum, with quantitative and health courses playing supporting roles.
alternatives.distinctness: Twelve courses differ from the integrated route: conservation, environmental observation, biogeochemistry, delta water and remediation, and sustainability research replace much of the molecular-laboratory and human physiology sequence.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offerings pass the enriched workbook. Introductory life, ecology, mathematics or sustainability courses precede relevant advanced work where scheduling permits; advisory progression has been reviewed.

alternatives.label: Molecular biology, disease and neuroscience
alternatives.concept: Examines cells, biochemical processes, genetics, infection and disease alongside the biological basis of brain function, physiology and data analysis. It follows the biomolecular and human-health interest without presenting general pharmacology as a replacement for the VU microbiology sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular life sciences, disease mechanisms, immune responses and neurobiology form a coherent majority of the completed curriculum.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses change from the integrated route and eighteen from the ecological one. Advanced pharmacology, immunity, disease, neural function and experimental methods replace several ecology, conservation and climate courses, producing a clear human and biomolecular emphasis.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 offerings pass the enriched workbook. Introductory life, ecology, mathematics or sustainability courses precede relevant advanced work where scheduling permits; advisory progression has been reviewed.

selection.assessment: The integrated living-systems route is the closest feasible UCR response; an ecology/evolution curriculum and a biomolecular/health curriculum arise from distinct target-specific interest clusters. All three concepts have relevant 24-course selections, pass formal feasibility and differ pairwise by at least six courses. Neuroscience and bioinformatics remain separately identified interests, but no fourth alternative is permitted.

notes.text: VU Biology requires both ecological field and biochemical laboratory work, microbiology and a 24-EC bachelor thesis, while it permits five credited second-year choices and a 30-EC open minor. UCR combines life science, ecology and data courses more flexibly, without claiming its general research or neuroscience courses reproduce the VU specialist microbiology, field placement or independent thesis.
